items.stem: Why is 'implicit none' recommended at the top of a modern Fortran program unit?

options.text: It forces every variable to be explicitly declared, catching typos at compile time
options.rationale: Correct: without it, undeclared names get implicit types and typos become silent bugs.
It has nothing to do with parallelism.

options.text: It switches the compiler to fixed-form source
options.rationale: Source form is independent of implicit none.

options.text: It makes all variables double precision
options.rationale: It does not change types; it requires explicit declaration.

items.explanation: Correct: without it, undeclared names get implicit types and typos become silent bugs.

items.stem: Which statements about Fortran arrays are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Arrays are stored in column-major order
options.rationale: Correct: the leftmost index varies fastest in memory.

options.text: Whole-array operations can replace explicit element loops
options.rationale: Correct: Fortran supports array-valued expressions and sections.

options.text: Arrays are stored in row-major order like C
options.rationale: Fortran is column-major, unlike C's row-major.

options.text: Array bounds must always start at 1
options.rationale: Lower bounds are configurable, e.g. dimension(0:9).

items.explanation: Correct: the leftmost index varies fastest in memory.; Correct: Fortran supports array-valued expressions and sections.

items.stem: What does iso_c_binding provide in modern Fortran?

options.text: Standardised interoperability types and conventions for calling between Fortran and C
options.rationale: Correct: it defines matching kinds and binding so Fortran and C can exchange data safely.
GPU offloading is a separate concern, not what the module provides.
It is about C interoperability, not testing.
Allocatables are managed by scope rules, not by this module.

items.explanation: Correct: it defines matching kinds and binding so Fortran and C can exchange data safely.
